newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA'S RULING SOCIALISTS APPROVE DOBREV FOR PM.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA'S RULING SOCIALISTS APPROVE DOBREV FOR PM.

text.p: Ruling Bulgarian Socialist Party (BSP) parliamentary allies on Wednesday approved nomination of Interior Minister Nikolai Dobrev as prime minister to replace outgoing Zhan Videnov after he resigned last month, a spokeswoman said.
President Zhelyu Zhelev is expected to hand Dobrev a mandate to form a new cabinet on Friday and then ask parliament within seven days to approve Dobrev's nomination and vote on the new cabinet.
Videnov resigned at a party congress on December 21, after months of criticism of his handling of the economy, sparking a showdown between party hardliners and reformists.
"Dobrev was a very good choice," BSP deputy Filip Bokov told Reuters.

Dobrev, 49, emerged as an outspoken critic of Videnov at the congress. He attacked the cabinet's record in handling Bulgaria's economic and social crisis and raised the previously taboo issue of government corruption.
The BSP is expected to discuss a new cabinet at a plenum on Sunday.
"Some of the ministers in the current cabinet will probably retain their posts in the new cabinet," said BSP's Lyubomir Kolarov.
A mining engineer by training, Dobrev was a leader of the Communist youth organisation Komsomol before 1989. He has also chaired parliament's national security committee.
Critics of his candidature say he lacks the economic background necessary to win the approval of Bulgaria's foreign partners.
